section.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar explains the difference between "receiving with a pleasant countenance" and "showing a smiling face," and how the latter reveals a higher, essential delight that transcends the arousal of repentance.
section.t: And it adds in the maamar, "and shows a smiling face to everyone,"
for the difference between "receives"
(with a pleasant countenance)
and "shows"
(a smiling face)
is,
that the term "receives" applies to something that exists beforehand
(before he received it)
and he receives that thing,
while "showing a smiling face" is that his smiling face
(which exists even before he shows it)
he shows and reveals to his fellow.
And this is that after it says that the king receives everyone with a pleasant countenance, it adds that he shows a smiling face to everyone,
for this that he receives them with a pleasant countenance is that the will of the people
(to greet the king)
is received by the king with a pleasant countenance,
and the addition of "shows a smiling face" is that when one is aroused in will to repent, there is drawn to him the revelation of the smiling face from above,
the delight
(laughter)
of the king himself.
For this delight is above the delight
(of the aspect of a pleasant countenance)
that comes from the arousal of repentance,
and as explained elsewhere,
that the root of laughter
(smiling face)
is in the essence of delight
(essential delight that is not composite)
which is above delight that comes through something
(composite delight).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The smiling face in the analogy refers to the delight in G-dliness inherent in Israel themselves, which when revealed, awakens in the person a corresponding essential delight in G-dliness, empowering complete repentance.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the matter of a smiling face in the analogue is the supernal delight that is in Israel themselves
(which is above the delight from the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos of Israel,
and above also the delight from the service of repentance)
for this delight is in the Essence [Atzmus].
And by his showing them a smiling face,
that this delight is revealed to the person
(who is aroused with a will to repent),
this awakens in him
(as in water, face to face)
the delight in G-dliness, until the delight in G-dliness is the very essence of his delight,
and this gives him even more strength to overcome obstacles and hindrances and to return in complete repentance.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: From the above it is understood that the revelation in Elul is not only a grant of power for service, but also awakens the person, yet the service in Elul is still "I am to my Beloved," the work of man.
section.t: And it must be understood,
that from the above it is understood that the revelation in Elul is not only a granting of power for service
[for when the king is in the field there is permission and ability for everyone to greet him]
but also awakens the person
[for by the king receiving everyone with a pleasant countenance, and especially by his showing a smiling face to everyone,
this awakens them to return in complete repentance],
and nevertheless the service in Elul is "I am to my Beloved,"
the service of man.
